diagnostic_evidence.quote:
by choosing a sufficiently large $\gamma$ and some proper  $\epsilon_{i}<1~(i=1,2,3)$,
we obtain (\ref{s2.18}).

issues.failure_explanation: The statement imposes no sufficiently-large-penalty condition. On a one-simplex mesh with beta zero, a nonconstant affine velocity has diffusion plus consistency contribution equal to minus mu times its squared gradient norm. Its penalty contribution tends to zero with gamma, so the asserted coercivity fails for sufficiently small positive gamma. The proof itself requires the missing hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and impose a mesh-independent threshold gamma greater than or equal to gamma_0, with the parameter dependencies required by the proof.
issues.overall_effect: Discrete well-posedness and the subsequent spectral estimates are not justified for an unrestricted penalty parameter.
issues.title: Discrete coercivity needs an unstated lower bound on the penalty
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard penalty threshold is a local hypothesis repair that preserves the intended method, parameter regimes, and convergence rates.

issues.failure_explanation: In dimensions two and three, general H1 functions do not have intrinsically defined nodal values. Changing a representative at interpolation nodes leaves its H1 equivalence class unchanged but changes its Lagrange interpolant. Thus the claimed operator on all of X does not exist.

failure_location.quote: Let $I_{h}: \mathbb{X}\to \mathbb{X}_{h}\cap C^{0}(\overline{\Omega})^{d}$ be the Lagrange interpolation operator.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the Lagrange interpolant to the continuous, sufficiently regular functions actually used, for example H0^1 intersected with H^{1+r} for r greater than one half.
issues.overall_effect: The interpolation construction has an invalid input-domain contract, although the later exact solutions have stronger regularity.
issues.title: The Lagrange interpolation operator is undefined on its declared domain
issues.why_classification: The source already assumes the regularity needed for its actual interpolation applications, so a local domain restriction preserves all substantive estimates.

issues.failure_explanation: Taking p equal to one, an allowed input, the elementwise projection conditions force vartheta_h p to equal one on every element. This contradicts its asserted membership in the mean-zero space W_h. The domain, codomain, and moment conditions are incompatible.

failure_location.quote: Let $\vartheta_{h}:~H^{s}(\Omega)\rightarrow \mathbb{W}_{h}$ be the local $L^{2}$ projection operator

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the local projection from L0^2 into W_h, or define it on all L2 with an unconstrained piecewise-polynomial range and note that it preserves zero mean.
issues.overall_effect: The stated projection is not a well-defined construction on its advertised domain.
issues.title: The pressure projection cannot map arbitrary inputs into the mean-zero space
issues.why_classification: All pressure inputs needed by the analysis are mean zero, so correcting the projection contract requires no change to the approximation rates or method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We use $h_{F}$ to denote the measure of $F\in \mathcal{E}_{h}$.

issues.failure_explanation: In three dimensions, the stated definition gives h_F comparable to h_tau squared. The projection only enforces normal continuity, so its tangential jumps are penalized with h_tau^{-2}, rather than the h_tau^{-1} scaling needed for the asserted H1-to-DG stability. Scaling a fixed patch input with a nonzero projected tangential jump makes the ratio in (s2.35) grow like h^{-1/2}. Independently, the face interpolation estimate (s3.2) requires the square root of a face length, not the square root of its area.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a face length scale, such as diam(F) or |F|^{1/(d-1)}, consistently in the penalty, norms, interpolation estimates, and residual indicators.
issues.overall_effect: The three-dimensional uniform inf-sup argument, the stated approximation rates, and the face-residual reliability argument do not follow for the area-weighted construction actually defined.
issues.title: Face area is used where the three-dimensional analysis requires a length
issues.why_classification: A consistent local correction of the face-size convention restores the scaling already used by the proofs without excluding three dimensions or changing the advertised rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $q$ be the algebraic multiplicity of $\lambda$, $\lambda=\lambda_{k}=\lambda_{k+1}=\cdots =\lambda_{k+q-1}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Normalization and a common eigenvalue index do not ensure a nonzero left-right pairing. At a defective eigenvalue, a right eigenvector lying in the range of T minus its eigenvalue is orthogonal to every corresponding ordinary adjoint eigenvector. At a multiple semisimple eigenvalue, independently selected normalized left and right eigenvectors can also be orthogonal. The proved identity only bounds the eigenvalue error multiplied by this pairing; the uniform division is unsupported under the lemma's hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Applying the same argument as in Lemma 5 in \cite{Wang2024}, we deduce that $|(\mathbf{u}_{h},\mathbf{v}_{h})|$ has a positive lower bound uniformly with respect to $h$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict these single-eigenpair arguments to simple isolated eigenvalues with coherently paired left and right eigenvectors and sufficiently small h. Retain only the independently supported subspace and mean-eigenvalue conclusions for general multiplicity unless a generalized-eigenspace argument is supplied.
issues.overall_effect: The individual eigenvalue estimates based on this lemma, particularly the unqualified a posteriori eigenvalue result and its cluster extension, are not established. The separately derived invariant-subspace and mean-eigenvalue estimates do not resolve this pairing problem.
issues.title: The eigenvalue identity is divided by an unjustified uniformly nonzero pairing
issues.why_classification: The directly supported repair withdraws the individual guarantees for defective and unrestricted multiple eigenvalues. Preserving that scope requires a substantially different spectral argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper specifies normalized eigenpairs but does not choose an exact eigenfunction matched to each discrete eigenfunction. Both (u_h,p_h) and (-u_h,-p_h) satisfy the same normalization and eigenproblem, but they cannot both converge to a fixed normalized u. For a multiple eigenvalue there is also an arbitrary basis rotation. Spectral subspace convergence does not imply the displayed estimates for unspecified fixed representatives.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Explicitly select exact eigenfunctions by a spectral-projection matching of each discrete eigenfunction, including phase normalization, and formulate the cluster comparisons for those matched representatives or for eigenspace distances.
issues.overall_effect: The individual primal and adjoint eigenfunction estimates and the cluster sums of raw eigenfunction differences are not valid with only the stated normalization.
issues.title: Eigenfunction errors are asserted without matching phases or eigenspace representatives
issues.why_classification: A contained eigenspace-matching construction preserves the approximation rates and spectral regimes, but scalar normalization alone cannot repair the multiple-eigenvalue comparisons.

issues.failure_explanation: For e_j=(T-T_h)u_j, Galerkin orthogonality involves the primal pressure error (S-S_h)u_j. The second equality in (s2.88) instead subtracts a term containing (S*-S_h*)u_i*. No stated equation makes A_h(e_j,I_h T*u_i*) plus that displayed pressure term vanish. Consequently the cancellation used to obtain the h^{2s} bound is invalid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the primal pressure error (S-S_h)u_j in both inserted pressure terms, apply the actual primal Galerkin orthogonality, and then use the already established source-problem estimates.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the h^{2s} mean-eigenvalue estimate contains an unsupported identity.
issues.title: The mean-eigenvalue proof uses the wrong pressure error in Galerkin orthogonality
issues.why_classification: The correction uses existing orthogonality and error estimates and preserves the stated mean-eigenvalue rate without a new lemma.

issues.failure_explanation: Substituting the adjoint interpolant into the eigenvalue identity leaves a diffusion term containing the gradient of u-u_h and DG trace terms. The available continuity and interpolation estimates bound this by h^r times the augmented DG error, not h^r times its L2 norm. No argument transferring or eliminating these derivatives is given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the velocity L2 error in (s2.90) by the augmented DG error and use the resulting h^r-small energy-error term in the subsequent absorption argument for sufficiently small h.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed justification of the source-to-eigenfunction comparison (s2.91), and hence the estimates derived from that comparison, is incomplete.
issues.title: The eigenvalue estimate unjustifiably replaces an energy error by an L2 error
issues.why_classification: The weaker, justified estimate is sufficient for the later absorption and preserves all advertised convergence rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the adjoint problem (\ref{s4.4})-(\ref{s4.5}) is equivalent to the adjoint problem (\ref{s2.48})-(\ref{s2.49}).

issues.failure_explanation: The original bilinear form has penalty gamma/h_F, whereas the alternative adjoint form has mu gamma/h_F. Integration by parts does not alter this term. Their difference contains (1-mu) times the jump-penalty pairing and is generally nonzero. Algorithm 1 therefore does not compute the asserted discrete adjoint when mu differs from one.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the extra factor mu from the alternative penalty, or explicitly rescale its penalty parameter by 1/mu.
issues.overall_effect: The adjoint eigenpairs produced by the stated adaptive algorithm need not satisfy the adjoint equations assumed by the theoretical estimator guarantees. The experiments with mu equal to one do not expose the discrepancy.
issues.title: The alternative adjoint solver uses a different penalty when mu is not one
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the alternative solver restores exact adjoint equivalence without changing the claimed rates or viscosity regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
By using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for each term on the right-hand side of (\ref{s3.30}),
and by (\ref{s3.24}) and Proposition 3.37 in \cite{Verfurth2013}, we get (\ref{s3.25}).

issues.failure_explanation: The last face integral in (s3.30) does not yield the claimed gradient-only local bound. A trace estimate introduces a local L2 velocity-error term, or an explicit velocity-jump term. Neither is present in (s3.25). Broken gradients cannot control jumps of piecewise constant offsets, and no local zero-mean condition or additional discrete argument is supplied. The same omission affects the adjoint face bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the local gradient seminorm by the full local H1 error, or add the appropriately weighted velocity-jump contribution, and retain that contribution when summing. The existing global DG norm can absorb these added terms.
issues.overall_effect: The local face-efficiency estimates are unsupported, and the global efficiency theorem relies on those estimates as stated.
issues.title: The local face-efficiency proof drops an uncontrolled convective jump
issues.why_classification: This requires a genuine weakening and repair of the local estimate, but the global efficiency guarantee can be retained through a contained trace argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and up to the oscillation terms, we can obtain the following corollary.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited eigenvalue theorem supplies an estimator bound plus exact-eigenfunction interpolation remainders. No estimate controls those remainders by the residual indicators or proves that they are negligible. For the allowed case k=r=1, the velocity remainder on a quasi-uniform mesh is h^2 times the squared H2 seminorm of u, since the affine interpolant has zero second derivatives; this is the same order as the claimed eigenvalue error. Calling the omitted terms oscillation does not establish the displayed estimator-only inequality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the summed primal and adjoint interpolation remainders from Theorem th3-8 in the corollary. An estimator-only result instead needs a substantive additional argument bounding those remainders.
issues.overall_effect: The residual-only reliability guarantee for cluster eigenvalues is not established, even after repairing the spectral pairing issues.
issues.title: The cluster eigenvalue bound discards uncontrolled interpolation remainders
issues.why_classification: The directly supported correction replaces the asserted computable estimator-only guarantee by a bound containing unknown exact-eigenfunction approximation terms, changing an important guarantee type.
